summary.headline: The Trails Committee reviewed presentation materials and FAQ documents for Town Meeting regarding CPA funding for the Peninsula Trail footbridge.
summary.summary: The Trails Committee met on October 8, 2020, to prepare for Town Meeting. The primary focus was Warrant Article 4, which requests Community Preservation Act funding to construct a footbridge over Route 30, completing a connection between the Peninsula Trail and the Boroughs Loop Trail. Members discussed project cost breakdowns, safety issues regarding pedestrians on Route 30, and the status of state MassTrails grants.

topics.title: Peninsula Trail footbridge and Town Meeting preparation
topics.summary: The committee reviewed and finalized presentation slides and FAQ handouts for Warrant Article 4 at Town Meeting. Discussion focused on how Community Preservation Act funds serve as the local match for a potential MassTrails grant, the project's safety benefits in eliminating a dangerous gap on Route 30, and cost details.
key_details: Project connects the Peninsula Trail to the 33-mile Boroughs Loop Trail via a footbridge over Route 30.
Maximum project budget is $428,550, including contingency and engineering costs.
Core project cost (bridge construction and professional oversight) is $324,050.
Project relies on a potential $202,750 MassTrails grant requiring CPA matching funds.
Without CPA funding, the project and grant cannot proceed.
topics.outcome: Committee members finalized their presentation strategy and handout materials for distribution at Town Meeting and Heritage Day.
topics.why_it_matters: Residents will vote at Town Meeting on Community Preservation Act funds to build a critical pedestrian footbridge, improving safety and completing a major regional trail connection.

topics.title: Routine business and adjournment
topics.summary: The committee concluded its discussion and voted to adjourn the meeting.
